later_events.mechanism: further_exemption_by_new_order: Executive Order 11909 (signed 1976-03-31) is a later order that recites this order and grants the same person a further exemption from mandatory retirement; it neither revokes, amends nor shortens this order.

clauses.reason: The order exempts Walter C. Sauer, First Vice President and Vice Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the United States, from mandatory retirement for age under subsection (c) of section 8335 of title 5 of the United States Code until March 31, 1976. The order recites that he would become subject to mandatory retirement for age as of March 31, 1975. The order is a single command with one fixed term, so its own stated date is the first end: 1976-03-31, recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when that day begins, is 1976-03-30. The order was signed 1975-03-28. Later events: Executive Order 11909 of 1976-03-31, each a further exemption of the same person with its own term, recorded as a later event and not as an end of this order. No amendment, revocation or shortening of this order is held (searched below).

research_rationale:
EO 11847 (signed 1975-03-28) is a one-person exemption under section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code: Walter C. Sauer, First Vice President and Vice Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the United States, is exempted from mandatory retirement for age until March 31, 1976. The held Federal Register text of the order was read in full and is a single operative clause (the recital, the finding of public interest, and the exempting sentence). The order ends by its own terms on 1976-03-31 (inclusive; exclusive alternative 1976-03-30, owner ruling 2026-10-21 on until dates). Later events: Executive Order 11909 of 1976-03-31, each a further exemption of the same person with its own term, recorded as a later event and not as an end of this order. Searches judged adequate: U.S. Code and eCFR (no hit naming the order), the Office of the Federal Register disposition-note catalog, and the held-text search for the person's full name, which found the chain members recorded above and nothing else. Whether the person left office on or before the stated date is not in any held source and is not asserted.

savings.reason: The exemption only suspended compulsory retirement for the stated term; it creates no continuing duty, office or rule. The person's service during the term and the pay for it had accrued by 1976-03-31; nothing in the order survives that date, and any later exemption is a separate grant recorded as a later event.
